title: Volume 5 · Journals, Accruals and the Bank
subtitle: Lessons 1–4: the four journal situations a consultant meets every month, and a bank reconciliation that closes to zero
outcomes: Post accruals and prepayments that reverse cleanly in the next period
Read any journal entry and say which reports it will move
Reconcile a bank statement to the ledger without a plug figure
Correct a misposting with a reversal or amendment rather than an edit

slides.title: Post an accrual that survives the close
bullets: An accrual records a cost in the month it was incurred, before the invoice arrives
The journal must name the same cost centre and cost type the invoice will later use
Use a dedicated accrued liabilities account, never the creditor control account
Every accrual needs a reversal date, or last month's cost is counted twice

rows: Electricity - SM, debit 800.00, cost centre Main - SM
TNB January bill not yet received

slides.notes: The accrual is not the hard part; the reversal is. Teach the learner to write the reversal date in the remark before submitting, because the person who reverses it in February is usually someone else. A dedicated accrued liabilities account also keeps the creditor control account honest, which matters the moment the client runs an ageing report and finds a supplier they never bought from.

slides.title: Read a journal the way an auditor does
bullets: A journal touches only the accounts you name, so nothing is hidden by a document type
Debits must equal credits before you look at any report
If a party is named, the entry moves the party ledger as well as the account
A journal that adjusts debtors directly is usually a workaround, not a correction
slides.notes: The fastest way to teach this is to ask which two reports move before the entry is submitted, then check. Expense up, liability up, profit down, cash untouched. A learner who can recite that for any journal is ready to sit in front of an accountant, because the accountant's first question is always which line changes.

slides.title: Release a prepayment month by month
bullets: A prepayment is an asset until the cover it buys is consumed
One twelfth per month is the discipline that keeps the balance sheet believable
Post the release as a journal, not by editing the original payment
Keep a schedule with twelve dates, because a spreadsheet is the audit evidence

rows: Insurance Premium 1,200.00 paid for twelve months
Journal: Dr Prepaid Insurance 1,200.00, Cr Insurance Expense 1,200.00
Journal: Dr Insurance Expense 100.00, Cr Prepaid Insurance 100.00
Same journal on the last day of each month
Eleven remaining, if starting in February
Twelve dated rows in the worksheet

slides.notes: Clients rarely object to the reclass, but they do object to eleven manual journals appearing every year. Show them the schedule first and agree who posts it, finance or the consultant, because an unposted release is the most common cause of a prepaid balance that never clears. If the amount is below the client's capitalisation threshold, say so and skip it.

slides.title: The prepaid schedule balances
bullets: The prepaid balance must equal the unexpired months multiplied by the monthly amount
Expense recognised so far plus remaining prepayment equals the original invoice
A prepayment with no schedule is a suspense account in disguise
Check the cost centre, because prepaid insurance is often split across branches
slides.notes: The identity here is the same shape as the stock identity, and that repetition is useful: whatever the topic, the proof is that the parts add to the whole. When a client's prepaid balance does not divide neatly into twelve, either the cover period is wrong or a month was posted twice, and both are five-minute fixes if caught in the same period.

slides.title: Reconcile the statement to the ledger, not to a plug
bullets: Reconciliation proves every line on the statement exists in the ledger, and vice versa
Unreconciled payments are usually timing, but two in a row means a real error
Use the bank reconciliation tool so the evidence is stored against each voucher
Agree the closing balance first, then work backwards through unmatched lines

rows: Statement and ledger side by side

slides.notes: Bank charges are the classic missing entry: the statement knows about them and the ledger does not, so the difference never clears by matching. Guide the learner to create the small entry rather than leaving a 35.00 variance, because a reconciliation with a plug figure teaches the client that the tool is decorative.

slides.title: What a clean reconciliation actually proves
bullets: Every statement line matched means cash is fully explained for the period
The reconciled ledger balance equals the statement balance at the cut-off date
Unpresented cheques and deposits in transit remain as timing differences, and they must be listed
A zero difference with matched lines is evidence, whereas a zero difference typed by hand is not

rows: Ledger balance at the same date

slides.notes: This is the one reconciliation a client will sign without argument, because the bank is the independent third party. Use it as the pattern for the others: start from the external document, prove every line, and list the timing differences rather than absorbing them. A consultant who can close a bank reconciliation in ten minutes is trusted with the rest of the close.

slides.title: Correct a mistake with a reversal, not an edit
bullets: Submitted entries are history, so the remedy is a reversal or an amendment with a trail
Cancelling a journal removes its ledger effect and leaves the document visible as cancelled
Amending keeps a link between versions, which is what an auditor reads
Never delete a document to fix a number, and never journal against a control account

rows: JE-SM-2026-0001, posted to the wrong cost centre
Amend, because the document is in an open period
From Retail Counter to Main - SM
Amendment recorded with a version history
Cancel and create a reversing journal

slides.notes: Give the learner both remedies and the rule that chooses between them: amend inside the open period, reverse once the period is closed or reported. What is never acceptable is deleting the document, because the gap it leaves is exactly what an auditor looks for. Say that sentence in the workshop and the client's finance team will repeat it.

slides.title: When a journal is the right document
bullets: Journals belong to adjustments, not to transactions that have their own document
If a purchase or sale happened, use the invoice; a journal hides the tax and the party
Accruals, prepayments, depreciation and corrections are the natural journal cases
Every journal needs a reason in the remark, because the next reader has no context

rows: Leave it unrecorded until the bill
Expense it all in month one

slides.notes: Consultants are tempted to solve awkward data with a journal because it is quick, and that is how control accounts end up with unexplained balances. This table gives the learner a defensible answer in the meeting: if the transaction happened, use its document; if only the timing happened, use a journal. The remark field is not optional either, since the next reader is usually the client's auditor.

lab.title: Lab · Accrue, prepay, reconcile the bank and correct a posting
steps: Post the 800.00 electricity accrual dated 31-01-2026 with a cost centre
Confirm profit falls by 800.00 and accrued liabilities rise by the same amount
Reclassify the 1,200.00 insurance premium to prepaid and release one month
Prove expense plus prepaid equals the original 1,200.00
Reconcile Bank - SM to a statement closing balance of 18,450.00
Create the 35.00 bank charge that the statement shows and the ledger does not
Take the reconciliation difference to 0.00 and save the evidence
Amend the misposted journal and confirm only the correct cost centre carries it
lab.done: Done when the accrual and the prepayment both reconcile to their identities, the bank reconciliation shows 0.00 difference with every line matched or listed, and the corrected journal has a version trail.

quiz.question: Why must an accrual carry a reversal date?
options: So the tax can be claimed
So the cost is not counted twice when the invoice arrives
So the party ledger stays clean
quiz.why: The invoice will post the same cost when it arrives, so the accrual must reverse in the following period to avoid double counting.

quiz.question: A 1,200.00 annual insurance premium is released monthly. What is the prepaid balance after one month?
quiz.why: One month of 100.00 is released, leaving 1,100.00 unexpired and sitting as an asset on the balance sheet.

quiz.question: The bank reconciliation shows a 35.00 difference caused by a bank charge. What is correct?
options: Create the bank charge entry in the ledger
quiz.why: The statement is the external evidence, so the missing bank charge belongs in the ledger. A plug figure destroys the value of the reconciliation.

quiz.question: A journal posted to the wrong cost centre in an open period. Best remedy?
options: Post a second journal to the opposite cost centre
quiz.why: Amending inside an open period keeps a version trail. Deleting destroys history, and a second journal leaves two wrong rows instead of one.

quiz.question: Which situation genuinely needs a journal rather than a document?
quiz.why: Depreciation has no external document, so a journal is its natural form. Sales, purchases and payments all have dedicated documents that also handle tax and parties.

memory.spine: Four journal situations recur every month, and each one has a reversal date that decides whether the next period is clean.

device.label: Accrue, prepay, reconcile, reverse
expansion: Accrual: the cost belongs to this month, the invoice arrives next month, and a reversal is set now
Prepayment: an asset until the cover it buys is consumed, released month by month
Reconciliation proves every statement line exists in the ledger and every ledger line on the statement
Corrections are reversals or amendments with a trail, never edits to a submitted entry

cards.a: On the reversal date set when it was posted, so the actual invoice lands cleanly in the next period.
cards.hint: Decide the date at posting time

cards.q: What is a prepayment before it is consumed?
cards.a: An asset: cover that has been paid for but not yet used.

cards.q: What does a clean bank reconciliation prove?
cards.a: That every statement line is matched to the ledger, so cash for the period is fully explained with no plug.

cards.q: How is a submitted journal corrected?
cards.a: Reverse it, or cancel and amend, because the trail is the whole point.

cards.q: Which four journal situations recur monthly?
cards.a: Accrual, prepayment release, depreciation and correction.

trap.what: A suspense account absorbs whatever the bank reconciliation cannot explain.
trap.why: Cash is then explained by an account nobody owns, and the balance grows every month until the close cannot be defended.

narration: Journals are where the accounting primer becomes a daily tool. An accrual records a cost before the invoice arrives, and it must reverse, or February carries January's electricity twice. A prepayment is an asset until the cover is used, so one thousand two hundred of insurance becomes one hundred a month, leaving one thousand one hundred on the balance sheet after the first release. Then the bank. Match every statement line, create the bank charge the ledger is missing, and drive the difference to zero with evidence rather than a plug. And when something was posted to the wrong place, amend it inside the open period or reverse it afterwards. Never delete, because the gap is exactly what an auditor looks for first. Practise the four situations until they are reflexes: accrual, prepayment, bank charge, wrong cost centre. Each one has a canonical remedy, and each remedy leaves a document behind, which is what turns a bookkeeping task into a consulting deliverable.
